answers.children: Yes — English Springer Spaniels are good with children because their affectionate and energetic nature makes them playful companions, though their boundless energy from flushing game birds can knock over toddlers during games of fetch. The medium build and loyal family-oriented temperament support gentle interaction when exercised adequately, yet their exuberance requires space to run. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 8/10)
answers.other-pets: Yes — English Springer Spaniels generally get along with other pets thanks to their sociable and affectionate temperament, though the high prey drive from retrieving game birds may spark chasing of smaller animals. Their intelligent and family-oriented traits help them live harmoniously in multi-pet homes when properly introduced, with loyalty extending to canine companions as well.
answers.exercise: English Springer Spaniels need 60 to 90 minutes of vigorous daily exercise such as long hikes, runs or intense fetch sessions that engage their keen nose and stamina developed for flushing and retrieving game birds all day. Without this their high energy leads to destructiveness like digging craters or chewing doorframes, as the breed was bred for boundless fieldwork enthusiasm.
answers.shedding: Yes — English Springer Spaniels shed moderately to heavily with seasonal bursts because their medium double coat traps loose hair that spreads around the house. The feathering on their legs and tails tangles easily from their energetic bounding through cover, increasing grooming demands for the working hunter build that still pulses in modern lines.
answers.hypoallergenic: English Springer Spaniels are not hypoallergenic. Their medium double coat sheds moderately to heavily and spreads loose hair and dander throughout the house, especially during seasonal blows that accompany their hunting heritage. They are rarely suggested to allergy sufferers because the combination of feathering on ears and legs with their energetic indoor movement keeps allergens circulating. No breed is genuinely hypoallergenic.
answers.training: Yes — English Springer Spaniels are easy to train because their intelligence, eagerness to please and high trainability stem from being bred to work closely with hunters flushing and retrieving game birds. The loyal and family-oriented temperament makes them responsive to consistent commands, though their energetic drive requires mental stimulation to prevent boredom-driven behaviours.
answers.lifespan: English Springer Spaniels live 12-14 years. Their health robustness is shaped by the stamina bred for long days in the field and the leaner build of field lines compared with show types that carry fuller coats, supporting an active life when their energetic needs are met.
answers.size: English Springer Spaniels reach 40-50 lb and stand 19-20 in tall at the shoulder. This medium substance gives them a sturdy yet agile build ideal for bounding through tall grass, feeling like a compact bundle of muscle and feathering that leans affectionately into laps despite the working hunter proportions.
answers.barking: English Springer Spaniels do not bark excessively. Their moderate barking level suits their role flushing and retrieving game birds where quiet focus matters, though the energetic and intelligent nature may produce alert sounds when bored or seeking interaction from their family-oriented temperament.
answers.apartment: No — English Springer Spaniels do not suit apartment living because their high energy from a history of flushing game all day leads to destructiveness and separation anxiety without 60-90 minutes of vigorous exercise. The affectionate and lively temperament struggles to settle indoors when mental stimulation for their keen nose is absent.
answers.first-time: No — English Springer Spaniels are not ideal as a first dog because their high energy can lead to destructiveness and separation anxiety if not exercised enough, demanding consistent training and grooming for the medium double coat. The exceptional hunting instincts and need for mental tasks challenge novices despite strong trainability and affection.
